title: Anchorage HealthTech Activation Kickoff & Integration Roadmap
summary: Kickoff for activation and integration of Redwood Inference. Discussed architecture options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), VPC/networking, security requirements (SAML, SOC2, KMS), initial pilot scope and success criteria. Agreed next steps: send security pack, share pricing/reserved capacity options, schedule staging run and benchmark with a 1k prompt set.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-24
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Anchorage CTO), Anya Ruiz (Anchorage Head of ML), Derek Owens (Anchorage DevOps), Casey Novak (Anchorage PO)

Autogenerated Summary (may be rough): kickoff + tech intake for activation, discuss options: hosted vs dedicated vs private, vpc routing, security doc ask, pilot scope and timeline.

[00:00] Jordan Mills: Alright hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intros round — then dive into the network and pilot plan. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account.
[00:22] Marcus Lee: Hey Jordan, Marcus here. Thanks, excited to kick this off. We've been looking at you folks for a while.
[00:30] Priya Raman: Hi all, Priya from SE — I'll own the bench‑marking and the staging run.
[00:38] Anya Ruiz: Anya here. We're most interested in inference latency for our clinical summarization flows and data residency.
[00:46] Derek Owens: Derek, infra. We'll be owning the VPC and peering setup, and I have some questions about private deployment modes.
[00:52] Jordan Mills: Great. Quick agenda: 1) confirm architecture choice and constraints 2) security/compliance asks 3) pilot scope & success criteria 4) next steps and timelines. Does that work?
[01:05] Casey Novak: Yep, sounds good.
[01:12] Marcus Lee: One ask up front: we need to avoid egress of PHI, so private deployment or VPC with strict peering is preferred.
[01:20] Priya Raman: Totally understood — looks like Anchorage wants either Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering or Redwood Private in their VPC; we can map both. A quick note: Dedicated will give you reserved capacity and easier SLAs, Private gives you full control of the control plane in your VPC.
[01:42] Anya Ruiz: How different is the runtime? Would we see different latency distributions between Dedicated and Private?
[01:50] Priya Raman: Runtime is the same engine but there are differences in network topology and kernel scheduling — Private in‑VPC avoids a hop to Redwood control plane, but Dedicated has predictable GPUs and autoscaling. For tight p50/p95 latency targets, Private can be slightly better but it depends on your infra.
[02:10] Marcus Lee: Okay — our initial target is p50 < 120ms for 512 token prompts and p95 < 400ms for 1k token prompts. Is that realistic?
[02:20] Priya Raman: Those are ambitious for the sequence lengths but doable with quantized model variants and prefix caching; we should run a benchmark with your real prompt set to validate.
[02:34] Jordan Mills: We'll plan a staging benchmark. Priya will run the harness, Marcus/Anya provide prompt sets and redaction rules.
[02:42] Derek Owens: For VPC peering, do you support Transit Gateway or only classic peering? We have TGW in our AWS account.
[02:53] Priya Raman: We support both; TGW is fine. We'll need your CIDR ranges and a point of contact. Also note our Private package uses a control plane that can be brought into your VPC via private link style or peering — some customers call it 'private control‑plane' so docs might show different names.
[03:12] Marcus Lee: Understood. Security — can you send over your SOC2 and a summary of your KMS/HSM options? We have vendor review next week.
[03:22] Jordan Mills: Yes, I'll share the security pack (SOC2, network diagram, KMS integration guide). We'll also include our encryption at rest defaults and keystore patterns.
[03:34] Anya Ruiz: Also SSO — we use SAML with SCIM provisioning, need RBAC for team roles.
[03:41] Priya Raman: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC is configurable. We'll attach a runbook for onboard admin flows.
[03:48] Casey Novak: What about logs/audit? We need to forward audit logs to Splunk for compliance.
[03:55] Priya Raman: We offer audit log exports and can forward syslog/HTTP ingest to your Splunk endpoint. For Private, logs stay in your environment; for Hosted we provide long‑term retention add‑ons.
[04:06] Marcus Lee: Good. Cost question — are there quick rules of thumb for Hosted vs Dedicated? We need to justify to finance.
[04:15] Jordan Mills: Hosted is usage-based — good for experimentation. Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable throughput and a committed monthly cost but lower unit token price. We'll share example TCOs.
[04:28] Anya Ruiz: Will you include an example where we run 10M tokens/month but with heavy short prompts versus long context?
[04:34] Jordan Mills: Yes, we'll include a model of mix and show both cost and latency tradeoffs.
[04:41] Derek Owens: On the networking side, do we need to open any outbound ports to Redwood? We're strict about egress.
[04:48] Priya Raman: For Dedicated with VPC peering, minimal egress — mostly health checks and control plane handshake; for Private, everything is inside your VPC. We'll include a network matrix in the security pack.
[05:00] Jordan Mills: Ok, pilot scope — the ask from Anchorage? Marcus?
[05:06] Marcus Lee: We want a 4‑week pilot: ingest ~1k clinical note prompts (anonymized), validate latency and hallucination metrics, measure cost, and test failover to a smaller model under load.
[05:20] Priya Raman: Perfect. For hallucination/quality we'll run evals with your ground truth and set regression alerts. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles that keep quality while lowering cost.
[05:33] Anya Ruiz: Will you allow model pinning during pilot? We want to lock a version.
[05:38] Priya Raman: Yes, pinning is supported and recommended during a pilot. We can do A/B and canary rollouts between variants.
[05:46] Casey Novak: What's the expected set up time for a Dedicated pool?
[05:51] Jordan Mills: For Dedicated, once contract's signed provisioning can be ~2‑3 weeks depending on region and capacity. Private is longer — typical on‑prem or VPC full control plane is 4‑6 weeks.
[06:04] Derek Owens: We may want to start Hosted to get initial metrics while Dedicated is provisioned. Is that common?
[06:10] Priya Raman: Very common — start on Hosted for quick validation, then migrate traffic to Dedicated with canary rollouts. We'll provide a migration plan.
[06:18] Marcus Lee: Ok, timeline wise finance will need final numbers by Oct 7th. Is that doable?
[06:24] Jordan Mills: We can aim for that. I'll get pricing to you by Sept 28th, demo of staging benchmarks the first week of Oct.
[06:32] Anya Ruiz: For the benchmarks — will your harness simulate concurrency? We care about tail latencies under load.
[06:38] Priya Raman: Yes, the harness can generate concurrent traffic and measure p50/p95/p99. We'll test different batch sizes to see the latency vs throughput tradeoff.
[06:47] Marcus Lee: Any data residency controls if we use Hosted? We need EU residency for some customers.
[06:53] Jordan Mills: Hosted offers region selection; we can pin to EU specific regions. For strict residency, Private in customer's region is the safest.
[07:03] Derek Owens: Ok network contact: I'll share infra@anchorage and a diagram. Expect a mail with CIDR and TGW details.
[07:11] Casey Novak: On the success metrics for the pilot, we should include qualitative reviewer scores for hallucination.
[07:17] Priya Raman: Good call — include a human eval rubric. We'll instrument it and feed alerts into your Slack channel.
[07:25] Jordan Mills: Great — a few admin notes: we'll need a list of users for SCIM and a staging API key request. Marcus, who will own procurement?
[07:34] Marcus Lee: I'll loop in our procurement lead but Casey will drive the pilot.
[07:40] Jordan Mills: Noted. Any blockers we haven't covered?
[07:44] Anya Ruiz: Only that we need to confirm redaction and de‑identification rules so the prompts are safe to send to Hosted if we start there.
[07:53] Priya Raman: We'll include a redaction checklist in the security pack.
[07:58] Jordan Mills: Ok let's talk specific timeline items and owners, then recap.
[08:04] Marcus Lee: Sounds good.
[08:07] Jordan Mills: Recap: Jordan send security pack + pricing by 2026‑09‑28; Priya schedule staging benchmark week of 2026‑10‑04; Anchorage to send CIDR and infra contact by 2026‑09‑26; Anya to deliver pilot criteria by 2026‑09‑29.
[08:22] Derek Owens: I'll get that CIDR info out today.
[08:26] Casey Novak: We'll prepare the pilot prompt set and annotation rubric.
[08:29] Jordan Mills: Excellent. Any final questions?
[08:32] Marcus Lee: A quick technical deep dive might be needed on memory/caching — can we plan a follow‑up SE session?
[08:39] Priya Raman: Yes, happy to do a technical deep dive on KV cache behavior, batching config, quantization impact. I'll propose times in the invite.
[08:50] Anya Ruiz: Also can you show how rollouts handle automatic fallback to smaller models under constrained capacity?
[08:56] Priya Raman: Yep we'll demo the rollout policy and fallback policy in the next call — we can run a simulated capacity constrain test.
[09:05] Jordan Mills: Alright I'll send invites for the follow up and share docs. Thanks everyone.
[09:12] Marcus Lee: Thanks all.
[54:30] [END] Note: timestamps between 09:12 and 54:30 omitted for brevity; call contained deeper technical q&a, network handshakes, and procurement logistics.
